claims.claim_text: The trend toward self-diagnosis through lab testing is growing in the US.
claims.reasoning: The article describes a private sector gearing up to serve the "test me" market and a biotech sector developing new testing products for well people.

citations.quote: A frothy private sector is gearing up to serve the "test me" market.
The biotech sector is excited about testing well people -- it's a huge market -- and is developing lots of new product.

claims.claim_text: The trend is motivated by a view to preempting disease.
claims.reasoning: The context describes testing well people and checking one's own lab values, but it does not state that the motivation is to preempt disease.

claims.claim_text: Over half of states allow walk-in and online lab services without a doctor's order.
claims.reasoning: The passage states that in states that allow this, and over half do, laboratories offer walk-in and online services for individuals to check their own lab values.

citations.quote: In those states that allow it -- and over half do -- laboratories are offering walk-in and online services to individuals who want to check their own lab values.

claims.claim_text: Critics argue that the trend is likely to lead to more medical care rather than improved health.
claims.reasoning: The passage argues that the primary effect will be more medical care, not more health.

citations.quote: But the primary effect won't be more health, but rather more medical care.

claims.claim_text: Patients present to doctors with abnormal results that are often false positives or minor abnormalities.
claims.reasoning: The passage says well people will appear with abnormal results, further testing often shows false alarms, and confirmed abnormalities are mostly minor.

citations.quote: Fundamentally well people will appear in doctors' offices with "abnormal" results.
Further testing will often make clear that the initial results were false alarms.
Or it will confirm the presence of abnormality -- most of which will be minor abnormalities.

claims.claim_text: Further testing can lead to increased anxiety, more procedures and over-treatment for diseases unlikely to cause problems.
claims.reasoning: The passage lists more anxiety, more procedures, and more treatment for disease not destined to cause problems as side-effects of testing the well.

citations.quote: Decades of research have shown that there are real side-effects to testing the well: more anxiety (that can't be good for your health), more procedures (which often involve needles, pain and can even lead to complications like collapsed lungs) and more treatment for "disease" not destined to cause problems

claims.claim_text: The trend is likely to increase healthcare costs through additional testing volume and subsequent office visits for abnormal results.
claims.reasoning: The passage says advertising will drive up testing volume, there will be office visits and subsequent testing for abnormal results, and this will cost people real money.

citations.quote: But advertising will drive up the volume of testing.
And then there are all the office visits and subsequent testing for the abnormal results.
This will cost people real money -- either in terms of higher insurance premiums or higher out-of-pocket costs.

claims.claim_text: Diagnostic tests can be extremely useful in sorting out acute medical problems.
claims.reasoning: The passage directly states this.

citations.quote: Diagnostic tests can be extremely useful in sorting out acute medical problems.

claims.claim_text: Diagnostic tests are not necessarily useful for routine check-ups.
claims.reasoning: The passage cautions that medical data can be very useful but are not necessarily routinely useful, and that testing well people will not make them feel better.

citations.quote: The public needs to know that while medical data can be very useful, that doesn't mean they are routinely useful.

claims.claim_text: The sector is in need of regulation.
claims.reasoning: The passage explicitly says this area demands regulation.

citations.quote: But it is certainly an area that demands regulation.

claims.claim_text: The public needs education about what test results indicate and how to respond to them.
claims.reasoning: The passage says the area demands education and that it is easier to collect data than to know what the data mean or what to do about the results.

citations.quote: It's also an area that demands education.
It is easier to collect data than it is to know what the data mean -- much less what to do about the results.
